the records say: Father *** WILLIAM TAYLOR ***, b. Feb 1826, cab driver and retired army sergeant; sons *** WILLIAM JOHN *** (b. Nov 1870) and *** HORACE ARCHIBALD *** (b. Apr 1872). *** THREE. ***
the photograph shows: *** THREE. *** An older man with full side-whiskers, seated at the right - identified by David as Mary Septima's father - and two young men, one seated at the far left and one standing at the centre-right.
what it means: *** AGREES EXACTLY, and the ages agree too. *** In 1890 the sons would be nineteen and eighteen, which is what the two young men look like, and the father sixty-four.

the records say: *** AGNES WALKER TAYLOR, born 3 August 1889 at 2 Fore Street *** - the youngest of the family and the only one small enough.
the photograph shows: One infant in white, on the lap of a seated woman at the centre. *** Sex cannot be told from the print. ***
what it means: *** THIS IS WHAT DATES THE PICTURE. *** If the infant is Agnes, the sitting is *** AFTER AUGUST 1889 ***. Mary Septima, identified as the small girl at the right, looks five - she turned five in September 1889. *** And by the census of 5 April 1891 both Isabella and Mary Septima are ABSENT from the house ***, so a sitting with everyone present most likely falls between *** August 1889 and early 1891. ***

what: *** FEMALES - AND THIS IS THE WHOLE QUESTION ***
the records say: Mother *** MARY ANN HELLEN *** (b. c.1843, London, St Bartholomew's) and the daughters the birth index confirms: *** KATHLEEN GEORGINA *** (1870), *** ISABELLA TEMPLE *** (1874), *** MARGARET HELLEN WALKER *** (1876), *** IRENE *** (1879), *** LUCY ELIZABETH *** (1881), *** MARY SEPTIMA *** (1884) - six, apart from the infant. *** With the mother, SEVEN. ***
the photograph shows: *** EIGHT ***, apart from the infant. Counted twice at full resolution, head by head: one markedly older in a bonnet and fringed shawl, seated; one seated in a white lace collar with the infant on her lap; and six more, from a small child to grown young women.
what it means: *** THERE IS ONE FEMALE IN THE FRAME THAT THE NAMED FAMILY DOES NOT ACCOUNT FOR. *** And the tree has always said *** TEN children *** while naming only nine. The birth index offers exactly one candidate for the tenth: *** TAYLOR, Edith, Bideford, September quarter 1882, 5b/506 *** - born precisely in the gap between Lucy (1881) and Mary Septima (1884), which is where a seventh daughter has to be if *** SEPTIMA *** is to mean what it says.

what: *** AND THE OTHER READING, WHICH IS DAVID'S AND IS NOT DISPOSED OF ***
the records say: The 1891 return for this house records *** AGNES HARRISON, VISITOR, 28, a dressmaker from Macclesfield *** - proof that women who were not daughters were in this household. And *** GEORGINA BRAYLEY, the grandmother ***, was alive and living alone in *** THE ALMS HOUSE, NORTHAM ***, aged 77, in the same parish.
the photograph shows: Two seated adult women, not one. The elder, in the bonnet and shawl, could be a woman of fifty or of seventy-five; the print will not say.
what it means: *** IF ANY ONE OF THE EIGHT IS A GRANDMOTHER, AN AUNT, A SISTER-IN-LAW, A VISITOR OR A SERVANT, THE COUNT IS SATISFIED WITH NINE CHILDREN AND NO EDITH. *** David said he thought there was a grandmother or an aunt in the group, and the parish records put a grandmother a few streets away. *** THE PHOTOGRAPH CANNOT CHOOSE BETWEEN THE TWO READINGS. *** What it has done is reduce the question to a single binary and name both sides of it.

the records say: Not a census: *** Mary Septima is missing from the whole of FreeCEN's Devon in 1891 ***, and so is any Edith of her age at Northam. The birth index gives no mother's maiden name until September 1911.
what it means: *** A BAPTISM REGISTER. *** Northam and Bideford parish baptisms name the parents, and would attach or detach the 1882 Edith in one line. That is the next record to open, and it has not been opened. *** A photographer's imprint on the mount would also date the sitting *** and is worth asking David for - the supplied image is cropped to the print.
